items.title: Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age
items.author: Timothy P. Padera
items.content: Menzel and colleagues report that male mice and humans undergo accelerated immune aging, characterized by naive CD8+ T cell decline and early thymic involution, which impairs cancer antigen recognition and response to immunotherapy.

items.title: Naive T cell decline limits cancer immunity in middle-aged male mice
items.content: Using mice and supporting human data, we show that accelerated loss of naive CD8+ T cells in male mice leads to lymph node contraction and limited cancer antigen recognition. Restoring thymic output replenished naive CD8+ T cells and improved responses to immunotherapy in middle-aged male mice.

items.title: Heterogeneity in secondary follicle development buffers the lifespan of activated oocytes to optimize female fertility in mice
items.author: Hua Zhang
items.content: Liang, Yang and colleagues map the developmental dynamics of activated oocytes and folliculogenesis across the reproductive lifespan using lineage tracing in mice. Their work reveals marked heterogeneity in the lifespan of activated oocytes in growing follicles, which form a secondary ovarian reserve that buffers oocyte utilization and sustains fertility.

items.title: Lipid elongation as a hallmark of aging
items.author: Shanshan Pang
items.content: Li and colleagues identify lipid acyl chain elongation as a conserved hallmark of aging across tissues and species. Genetic shortening of lipid chains extends lifespan in worms, which establishes chain length as a causal contributor to aging.
